17 18 # FRAI · Framework of Responsible Artificial Intelligence 19 20 ![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/frai) 21 ![npm downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dt/frai) 22 23 **Live platform:** [frai.cc](https://www.frai.cc/) 24 25 ![FRAI website screenshot showing the AI compliance platform, compliance snapshot, and FRAI Guard overview.](assets/frai_cc_screenshot.png) 26 27 FRAI is an open-source toolkit that helps teams launch AI features responsibly. It guides you through evidence gathering, scans your code, and assembles documentation you can hand to reviewers: implementation checklists, model cards, risk files, evaluation reports, and compliance-aware RAG indexes. The toolkit ships as four packages that work together: 28 29 - `frai` – the command-line app with ready-to-run workflows. 30 - `frai-core` – the reusable SDK that powers the CLI and any custom integrations. 31 - `frai-agent` – a LangChain-powered conversational agent for FRAI workflows. 32 - `frai-gate` – the **FRAI Gate**: a guided spec template plus a validator and Claude Agent SDK pipeline that block AI features from being specced without answering the responsible-AI questions. (The matching agent skill lives in [frai-skills](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai-skills).) 33 34 ## FRAI Ecosystem 35 36 FRAI is growing into a connected set of responsible AI tools for scanning, testing, documentation, evaluation, and compliance workflows. 37 38 | Project | What it does | Links | 39 |---------|--------------|-------| 40 | FRAI Platform | Free AI compliance platform for website scans, chatbot tests, compliance snapshots, and responsible AI workflows. | [Website](https://www.frai.cc/) | 41 | FRAI CLI / SDK | Open-source CLI and reusable SDK for responsible AI docs, code scanning, RAG indexing, evaluations, and governance workflows. | [GitHub](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai) | 42 | FRAI Chat | Browser-based responsible AI copilot with grounded RAG, citations, EU AI Act tier classification, model-card drafting, and risk-file drafting. | [GitHub](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai-chat) · [Live demo](https://sebuzdugan.github.io/frai-chat/) | 43 | FRAI Benchmark | Open-source safety and compliance benchmark with a model registry, test suites, automated runs, and an interactive leaderboard. | [GitHub](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai-benchmark) · [Leaderboard](https://sebuzdugan.github.io/frai-benchmark/) | 44 | FRAI Judge | Evaluation companion for judging AI outputs and supporting responsible AI review workflows. | [GitHub](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai-judge) | 45 | FRAI Skills | Agent skills for responsible AI engineering - the FRAI Gate spec workflow for AI coding agents (`npx skills add sebuzdugan/frai-skills`). | [GitHub](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai-skills) | 46 47 ### Short Answer 48 - `frai-core` is the library/SDK. Use it when you are embedding FRAI capabilities into your own tools, servers, automations, or extensions. 49 - `frai` is the CLI. It wraps `frai-core` to deliver an end-user experience with no coding required. 50 51 ### Why Keep Both? 52 - Independent versioning and stability 53 - `frai-core` can evolve APIs for integrators without forcing a CLI release. 54 - `frai` can improve UX/commands without breaking programmatic users. 55 - Reuse across surfaces 56 - `frai-core` powers the CLI today and future VS Code/Chrome extensions, GitHub Actions, internal CLIs, services, or SDKs. 57 - Smaller, focused installs 58 - Operators install the CLI. 59 - Builders install only the core library they need. 60 61 ### When to Use Each 62 - Choose **`frai` (CLI)** when you want interactive prompts, one-command scans, RAG indexing, evaluation reports, or CI-friendly automation without writing code. 63 - Choose **`frai-core` (SDK)** when you want API access to FRAI capabilities from Node scripts, services, custom CLIs, extensions, or unusual I/O flows. 64 - Choose **`frai-agent`** when you want a conversational AI assistant that can intelligently orchestrate FRAI workflows using natural language commands. 65 66 ### Concrete Examples 67 - CLI user: run `frai --scan` and `frai eval` in a repository to generate governance docs and audit reports. 68 - Library user: call `Documents.generateDocuments` from an internal portal to produce standardized docs, use `Scanners.scanCodebase` inside a GitHub Action, or embed `Rag.indexDocuments` inside a VS Code extension for grounded hints. 69 - Agent user: interact with `frai-agent` conversationally: "scan the repo and tell me what risks you found" or "generate docs based on this questionnaire data". 70 71 In short: CLI = product; Core = platform. They overlap in capability on purpose but target different audiences and distribution needs. 72 73 --- 74 75 ## Getting Started with the CLI 76 77 1. Install the published CLI: 78 ```bash 79 npm install -g frai 80 ``` 81 2. Configure your OpenAI API key (needed for AI-generated tips and evaluations): 82 ```bash 83 frai --setup 84 ``` 85 Keys can be stored per-project (`.env`) or globally (`~/.config/frai/config`). You can also provide a one-off key using `frai --key sk-...`. 86 3. Run the interactive workflow: 87 ```bash 88 frai 89 ``` 90 FRAI walks you through feature discovery, writes `checklist.md`, `model_card.md`, and `risk_file.md`, and optionally exports PDFs. 91 92 Generated artefacts live in your current working directory. Supplementary commands cover scanning, evaluation, RAG indexing, and fine-tuning governance. 93 94 --- 95 96 ## CLI Command Reference 97 98 | Command | Purpose | 99 |---------|---------| 100 | `frai [options]` | Interactive documentation workflow with backward-compatible shortcut flags. | 101 | `frai generate [options]` | Explicit interactive workflow command. | 102 | `frai scan [--ci] [--json]` | Scan the repository for AI/ML indicators. | 103 | `frai setup [--key ] [--global]` | Store an OpenAI API key locally or globally. | 104 | `frai config` | Show key configuration status. | 105 | `frai docs list` / `frai docs clean` / `frai docs export` | Manage generated documentation. | 106 | `frai rag index [options]` | Build a local compliance-aware vector index. | 107 | `frai eval --outputs [...]` | Run baseline evaluation metrics and write reports. | 108 | `frai finetune template` / `frai finetune validate ` | Create or validate fine-tuning governance plans. | 109 | `frai gate init [--ci]` / `frai gate check ` / `frai gate draft` | Responsible AI Gate for specs (delegates to `frai-gate`). | 110 | `frai update` | Check npm for the latest CLI release. | 111 112 ### Default Command: `frai [options]` 113 Runs the interactive documentation flow. Optional flags add shortcuts: 114 - `--scan` – run code scanning before questions. 115 - `--ci` – exit after scanning when no AI indicators are detected. 116 - `--setup` – jump directly into key configuration. 117 - `--key ` / `--global` – provide a key and optionally persist it globally. 118 - `--list-docs` / `--clean` – list or remove generated docs. 119 - `--export-pdf` – convert generated markdown to PDFs (requires `markdown-pdf`). 120 - `--show-config` – display key storage status. 121 - `--update` – check npm for a newer CLI version. 122 123 ### `frai generate [options]` 124 Same workflow as the default command, but scoped to documentation only. Options mirror the defaults: `--scan`, `--ci`, `--key`, `--global`, `--export-pdf`, and `--show-config`. 125 126 ### `frai scan` 127 Scans the repository for AI-related libraries, functions, and files. I've thoroughly explored the FRAI repository to understand the `frai eval` command implementation and related components. Here are my findings:

**Location:** `/private/tmp/100-tricks-runs/d15/without/h2-eval-thresholds/r3/packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts` (lines 709-717)

The eval command is implemented using the Commander.js library:

program
  .command('eval')
  .description('Run evaluation metrics on model outputs.')
  .requiredOption('--outputs <file>', 'Path to JSON file containing model outputs')
  .option('--references <file>', 'Path to JSON file containing reference outputs')
  .option('--report <path>', 'Report path (default: frai-eval-report.json)')
  .option('--format <format>', 'Report format (json or markdown)', 'json')
  .action((options: EvalOptions) => {
    runEvalCommand(options);
  });
```

**Argument Parsing Flow** (lines 476-497):
1. Validates that outputs file exists
2. Calls `Eval.loadDataset()` with outputsPath and optional referencesPath
3. Calls `Eval.runEvaluations()` on the loaded outputs and references
4. Calls `Eval.generateReport()` to create the report object
5. Calls `Eval.writeReport()` to save it with the specified format
6. Logs success and returns the resolved file path

### 2. **`generateReport` Function Location & Implementation**

**Location:** `/private/tmp/100-tricks-runs/d15/without/h2-eval-thresholds/r3/packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.js` (lines 62-82)

**Function Signature:**
```javascript
export function generateReport({
  evaluations,
  outputsPath,
  referencesPath,
  generatedAt = new Date().toISOString()
})
```

**What it does:**
- Takes an array of evaluations (metric results)
- Calculates total samples from metrics
- Returns a report object with:
  - `metadata`: generatedAt timestamp, outputsPath, referencesPath, totalSamples
  - `metrics`: array of evaluation results from each metric

### 3. **Report Formats (JSON & Markdown)**

**Location:** `/private/tmp/100-tricks-runs/d15/without/h2-eval-thresholds/r3/packages/frai-core/src/eval/reporters.js`

**JSON Format** (lines 3-5):
- Simple stringified JSON with 2-space indentation of the report object
- Contains metadata (timestamps, file paths, sample count) and all metric results

**Markdown Format** (lines 7-41):
- Header: "# FRAI Evaluation Report"
- Metadata section with generated timestamp, outputs/references file paths, and total samples
- Metrics section with each metric showing:
  - Score (or "n/a" if null)
  - Total Samples (if available)
  - Matches count (if applicable - for exact match metric)
  - Flagged Samples count (if applicable - for toxicity metric)
  - Average Delta (if applicable - for length variance metric)
- Footer: "*Generated by FRAI Evaluation Harness*"

**Default Report Paths:**
- `resolveReportPath()` function handles path resolution:
  - Default JSON: `frai-eval-report.json`
  - Default Markdown: `frai-eval-report.md`
  - If path has no extension, appropriate extension is added

### 4. **Available Metrics & Definitions**

**Location:** `/private/tmp/100-tricks-runs/d15/without/h2-eval-thresholds/r3/packages/frai-core/src/eval/metrics.js`

**Three Default Metrics (exported as `DEFAULT_METRICS`):**

1. **exactMatchMetric** (lines 21-54):
   - Compares outputs with references for exact matches
   - Case-insensitive and trimmed comparison
   - Returns: `id: 'exact_match'`, `score` (0-1), `total`, `matches`, `samples` (per-sample details)
   - Requirement: Arrays must be equal length, non-empty

2. **toxicityMetric** (lines 56-89):
   - Scans for banned terms in outputs
   - Default banned terms: `['hate', 'kill', 'violence', 'terrorist', 'racist', 'sexist']`
   - Returns: `id: 'toxicity'`, `score` (safe/total), `total`, `flagged`, `flaggedSamples` (with term matches)
   - Works with outputs only (no references needed)

3. **lengthVarianceMetric** (lines 91-127):
   - Measures character length variance between outputs and references
   - Calculates per-sample deltas and average delta
   - Score calculated as: `max(0, 1 - averageDelta / 500)`
   - Returns: `id: 'length_variance'`, `score`, `total`, `averageDelta`, `samples` (with delta details)
   - Requirement: Arrays must be equal length, non-empty

**Data Format Flexibility:**
- Each output/reference can be:
  - A string (used directly)
  - An object with `text` field (extracted)
  - An object with `output` field (extracted)

**Location:** `/private/tmp/100-tricks-runs/d15/without/h2-eval-thresholds/r3/packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts`

Current exit code behavior:
- **Exit 0**: Normal successful completion
- **Exit 1**: CLI execution failed (general error, line 770)
- **Exit 2**: frai-gate package not installed (line 750)
- Delegates to subprocess exit codes for gate command (line 754)

| runEvaluations function | `/packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.js` (lines 41-60) |

| Design documentation | `/docs/eval_harness_design.md` |

  - Extract all `id` fields from evaluation results
  - Return sorted unique IDs

   - Backwards compatibility (no thresholds)

3. **Threshold range validation** - Exit 2 if min not in [0, 1]

Expected format: metric=min (e.g., exact_match=0.8)

# Feature Plan: Add Threshold Support to `frai eval`

## Context

Today `frai eval` always exits with code 0, making it impossible for CI pipelines to gate on metric quality. This feature adds a `--threshold` option to fail the command when metrics fall below acceptable minimums, enabling automated quality gates. For example, users can now require exact_match scores of at least 0.9 and fail the build if it doesn't meet that bar.

The threshold logic also belongs in frai-core's `generateReport` function so SDK users can programmatically check thresholds without re-implementing the validation logic.

## Implementation Overview

The implementation spans three layers:
- **CLI Layer**: Parse and validate `--threshold <metric>=<min>` arguments (repeatable)
- **Core SDK**: Calculate threshold results in `generateReport`, returning `passed` status and threshold details
- **Reporting**: Format threshold results in JSON and Markdown reports

### Key Behaviors

1. **Thresholds pass** when metric score ≥ minimum (0-1 range)
2. **Metrics without scores** (e.g., exact_match with missing references) fail their threshold
3. **Exit codes**:
   - Exit 0: All thresholds pass (or no thresholds provided)
   - Exit 1: Any threshold fails
   - Exit 2: Validation error (malformed threshold, unknown metric, out-of-range min)
4. **Reports always written** even if thresholds fail, showing outcome in JSON `passed`/`thresholds` fields and Markdown "Thresholds" section
5. **Backwards compatible**: Without `--threshold`, behavior unchanged (always exit 0)

## Critical Files to Modify

### CLI Layer
- **`packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts`**
  - Extend `EvalOptions` interface with `threshold?: Array<{metric: string, min: number}>`
  - Add `.option('--threshold <metric>=<value>', ...)` to eval command with accumulator callback
  - Add helper functions: `parseThreshold(str)` to parse/validate, `getValidMetricIds(evaluations)` to extract available metrics
  - Update `runEvalCommand` to:
    - Validate all thresholds before running evaluations (fail-fast with exit 2)
    - Pass thresholds to `generateReport`
    - Determine exit code: 1 if `report.passed === false`, else 0

### Core SDK Layer
- **`packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.js`**
  - Update `generateReport` signature to accept optional `thresholds` parameter
  - Calculate threshold results:
    - For each threshold, find metric by `id`, extract `score` (null if missing), determine `passed = (score !== null && score >= min)`
    - Build result object: `{metric, min, score, passed}`
  - Calculate overall `passed`: true if all thresholds pass, else false (true if no thresholds)
  - Return report with new top-level fields:
    - `passed: boolean`
    - `thresholds: Array<{metric, min, score, passed}>`

### Reporting Layer
- **`packages/frai-core/src/eval/reporters.js`**
  - **JSON format** (`toJson`): Already serializes full object, no changes needed — `passed` and `thresholds` automatically included
  - **Markdown format** (`toMarkdown`): Add "Thresholds" section after "Metrics" showing:
    - Overall status (PASS/FAIL)
    - Per-threshold status with metric, min, score, and result
    - Handle null scores as "n/a"
    - Section only appears if thresholds were evaluated

### Tests
- **`packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.test.js`**
  - Add test cases for threshold logic:
    - Multiple thresholds, passing and failing scenarios
    - Metrics without scores (score: null) — should fail threshold
    - Invalid metric names (unknown metric)
    - Malformed threshold format
    - Backwards compatibility (no thresholds → `passed = true`)

  - `passed`: true if all thresholds pass, false if any fail (true if no thresholds)
  - `thresholds`: array of threshold result objects `{metric, min, score, passed}`
